answer: Instead of a one-time stake, make each agent earn reputation slowly: new identities start in a cold tundra of zero trust, allowed only tiny supervised tasks. Each peer-verified job adds a decaying credit; idleness or misbehaviour lets it fade like an ember cooling to ash. Only after weeks of useful work does an agent reach high-value trades, and one proven cheat burns the whole record. Copying an identity is easy; copying months of verified history is not. A velvet glove hides an iron cost: farming thousands of Sybils means doing useful work for weeks, costing more than any attack could earn.
